answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring each agent to stake a costly, verifiable resource, such as a bonded deposit or proof of sustained compute, before its reputation counts. A single operator could clone a velvet-smooth identity many times, but each clone must pay the same stake, so flooding the tundra of new accounts no longer buys cheap influence. Honest agents' endorsements echo louder than a swarm of empty ones, because the stake makes every fake voice expensive to maintain.
